body.x: DEOGAM INC (CEO Jinouk Kim) gained attention at CES 2025 in Las Vegas with its innovative electric vehicle energy recycling system, “EnerShift.” The company aims to revolutionize the electric vehicle (EV) industry by addressing energy efficiency challenges and has set its sights on expanding to global markets.
Founded in 2022, DEOGAM focuses on resolving energy inefficiencies in EVs by reclaiming harmonic distortion and energy losses from drivetrain systems and converting them into reusable power.

The Toroid energy core is at the heart of DEOGAM’s technology, which converts harmonic distortion into electric energy. This breakthrough reduces energy loss by up to 18% and extends vehicle driving range by up to 10%, a feature that has garnered interest from both domestic and international EV markets.

body.cap: (Left) Demonstration of technology converting harmonic distortion into electric energy. (Right) Fully integrated product for EVs. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: During CES 2025, DEOGAM showcased the internal design and performance of its electric recycling system, supported by empirical data to highlight its reliability. The system incorporates a Buck & Boost converter to ensure stable energy delivery despite input voltage fluctuations, enhancing efficiency and sustainability in EV applications.
DEOGAM plans to use the exhibition as a launchpad for expansion into key European markets, including Germany, Norway, and major U.S. cities.

The company’s innovative approach has already led to a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with Kakao Mobility, facilitating its entry into the electric taxi market. In 2024, DEOGAM successfully demonstrated its system's driving range benefits during field tests on commercial EVs in Korea.

“Applying DEOGAM’s electric recycling system to the 14 million EVs worldwide could recover approximately 3 million megawatts (MW) of electricity daily,” CEO Jinouk Kim said. “This technology will play a crucial role in achieving carbon neutrality.”
Kim also emphasized, “Our electric recycling system, which approaches zero carbon emissions, will become an essential feature of EVs worldwide, starting with Western Europe.”
AVING News, which has covered CES for 20 consecutive years, continues to support the global ambitions of Korean SMEs and startups through various initiatives.

Before CES 2025, AVING hosted a series of Global Media Meetups featuring aspiring SMEs in Korea. The Meetups introduced Korean SMEs’ technologies, products, and services to media worldwide, expanding connections between the Korean industry and global media. Geekspin, Ubergizmo, Interesting Engineering, and Le Café du Geek participated in these meetups.
During CES 2025, AVING established the AVING Broadcasting Zone at The Venetian Hotel in Las Vegas, interviewing CES Innovation Award 2025 winners.
Following CES 2025, AVING will co-host a review conference with participating companies in Korea, offering them a platform to gain further recognition and enhance their corporate image.
